name: IC-705
subtitle: Field reference
kicker: Independent reference. Not an Icom publication and not affiliated with Icom.
verified: Compiled from the Icom IC-705 Basic Manual, Advanced Manual and CI-V Reference Guide, September 2026. Not checked against a radio.
specs: HF amateur bands, plus 6 m, 2 m and 70 cm
USB, LSB, CW, RTTY, AM, FM, DV. WFM receive only
0.1 to 5 W, 0.025 to 1.25 W AM. The supply sets the ceiling, not a menu
13.8 V DC external, or 7.4 V from the BP-272 pack
Under 3 A at 13.8 V, under 2.5 A at 7.4 V
0.5 A at 13.8 V at full audio, 0.3 A in standby
None. The external AH-705 is driven from the tuner jack
Micro USB, plus built-in Bluetooth and wireless LAN
keys: Opens the settings tree, where the set items live.
The per-contact surface: AGC, split and the like. Separate from MENU.
Context menu for whatever is on the screen. Faster than MENU for most things.
Leaves a screen or steps back one level.
Push to open the multi-function menu, rotate to change the selected item.
Cycles VOX, or on CW cycles semi break-in, full break-in and off. Hold about a second to set the delay.
Tap turns the offset on and off. Hold swaps between receive and transmit offset.
Held, listens on the transmit frequency in split, or opens the squelch on simplex.
Tap opens scan select. Hold about a second restarts the last scan.
Tap steps the memo pad. Hold saves what is displayed into it.
Tap swaps call channel and VFO. Hold turns the D-STAR repeater function on or off.
Tap announces the frequency aloud. Hold locks the dial.
Push to swap PBT1 and PBT2, rotate to shift the passband, hold to clear.
Rotate for audio. Push to bring up its setting menu.
quick: Hold the PTT and push MULTI, then touch RF POWER. The scale is 0 to 100 per cent of whatever the supply allows.
Same multi-function menu, holding the PTT.
Multi-function menu. Roughly 6 to 48 words per minute.
On the FUNCTION screen. Touch to step fast, mid and slow. Touch and hold to set the constant per mode.
On the FILTER screen. Touch BW then rotate.
FUNCTION screen. Caps transmit power, which is worth setting for a small battery.
filters: Three filter settings per mode. Touch the filter icon to step them, or hold it a second to open the filter screen.
On the filter screen, touch BW and rotate to set the passband width of the selected filter.
Twin passband tuning. Push PBT to swap between them, rotate to shift, hold to clear.
tasks: 500 channels across 100 groups. From VFO mode, touch the VFO and memory icon, touch MW, choose to write to a new channel, pick it, confirm. Holding MW for a second writes straight into a blank channel in the group.
Touch the VFO and memory icon, then MEMO. Step channels with the up and down keys or the dial set to memory.
Push SCAN for the select screen, or hold it a second to restart the last scan.
Push FUNCTION, then touch SPLIT for one second. Quick split turns on and VFO A is copied to B.
Hold the PTT and push MULTI, touch RF POWER, rotate. Ten watts needs external power; on the internal pack the ceiling is five.
MENU, then set, then time set. The UTC offset is in the same branch.
MENU, set, others, reset. Partial reset clears settings and keeps your memory channels and the card. All reset takes the memories with it.
control: Micro USB Type-B on the side. It also charges and powers the radio.
With Icom's driver the radio presents two serial ports, one for CI-V and one for the second function.
A4h by default. Read off Icom's own CI-V frame examples rather than a sentence naming it, so confirm it in set mode.
Not needed. USB carries CI-V directly, unlike the older sets that want a CT-17.
Bluetooth and wireless LAN are built in, each with their own set branch.
notes: Ten watts needs external power. On the internal pack the radio makes five, which is a real difference on a marginal path and no difference at all on a good one.
BNC, not SO-239. Carry the adapter you actually need rather than discovering which one you left at home.
The battery is the single point of failure on a long activation. Know its state before you walk in and carry a way to charge or replace it.
It is a receiver with a touchscreen, so it will happily drain the pack while you look at the waterfall and call nobody.
There is no internal tuner. Whatever you put up has to be resonant or matched by something you carried in.
settings: CI-V address, as read from set mode
